job_title: AI / ML & Full-Stack Software Engineer (Graduate / Entry-Level)
pool_summary: The pool separates into a technically strong AI/research cluster with multimodal models, retrieval systems, publications, and selective international labs, and a product-engineering cluster with quantified user, engagement, and workflow outcomes. The clearest upper-echelon signals are measurable model quality, end-to-end retrieval/LLM construction, demonstrated product impact, selective research exposure, and externally validated technical output.

axes.label: Measured Multimodal Model Engineering
axes.rationale: This distinguishes candidates who moved beyond baseline ML coursework into active construction and measurement of meaningful computer-vision, NLP, or multimodal systems. Quantified performance and technically nontrivial architectures are concentrated among the strongest AI-oriented candidates in this pool.
axes.strong_criteria: Active ownership [action] of at least two substantial applied AI systems, or one technically advanced training/engineering effort, with explicit evaluation such as approximately 80%+ accuracy/F1, 80%+ mIoU, or a comparable benchmark; evidence should include named architectures, datasets, GPUs, or fine-tuning methods rather than only a model name.
axes.moderate_criteria: Active ownership [action] of one applied ML system with a named model family, dataset, or implementation mechanism but no quantified evaluation, or one quantified but relatively standard classifier/detector at project or internship scope. Peripheral participation or an unbacked tool listing does not qualify as moderate by itself.

axes.label: RAG, Search & LLM Systems
axes.rationale: Production AI work for this role benefits from understanding retrieval pipelines, semantic indexing, and LLM-facing system composition rather than isolated model training. Only a small subset of this pool shows active ownership of multi-stage retrieval or search architectures with concrete components.
axes.strong_criteria: Active ownership [action] of an end-to-end retrieval or LLM system using at least two concrete mechanisms such as embeddings, BM25, FAISS/vector indexing, semantic search, reranking, or retrieval evaluation; strongest evidence includes a working search/RAG product, domain-specific retrieval, or publication-quality implementation.
axes.moderate_criteria: Active ownership [action] of a search engine, LLM application, chatbot, or question-answering system using one meaningful retrieval/model-integration mechanism, such as semantic search, ChatGPT API integration, transformer table answering, or a prompt assistant, without evidence of a full retrieval pipeline or evaluation.

axes.label: Quantified Product Engineering Impact
axes.rationale: The full-stack side of the role requires turning software into usable products, and several contenders demonstrate this through adoption, concurrency, retention, conversion, or operational outcomes. These measurable results separate product ownership from merely listing frameworks or completing undifferentiated applications.
axes.strong_criteria: Active ownership [action] of a product or production-facing system with at least one concrete scale or outcome signal at the upper end of this pool—approximately 100+ daily users, 100 concurrent users, or two quantified product outcomes such as retention, engagement, bounce, onboarding, or processing-time improvement.
axes.moderate_criteria: Active ownership [action] of a complete web, mobile, real-time, or workflow application with clear user-facing functionality, but without quantified adoption or business impact; quantified results below the strong thresholds or contribution to a larger system also qualify as moderate.

axes.label: Selective Research Environment Exposure
axes.rationale: The job explicitly values selective labs and international experience, and this pool contains a small cluster with exposure to DFKI, Lakehead, UC Davis, GSoC, and distinguished exchange programs. The differentiator is substantive technical ownership in those environments, not simply attendance or a generic internship title.
axes.strong_criteria: Verified work-history or header evidence of active technical work [action] in a selective international research environment, major open-source program, or distinguished exchange, with a concrete engineering or research contribution; examples include DFKI/Lakehead/UC Davis research, GSoC, or a distinction-backed international exchange.
axes.moderate_criteria: Verified research or engineering experience in a university lab, research internship, or comparable structured environment with an active technical contribution [action], but without clear international selectivity, major-program distinction, or evidence of advanced research scope.

axes.label: Externally Validated Technical Output
axes.rationale: Publications, funded research, and open-source traction provide independent validation beyond classroom or internship claims and are unusually concentrated among the strongest research-oriented contenders. This axis measures the external artifact or recognition itself, while remaining distinct from the environment in which the work occurred.
axes.strong_criteria: Active ownership [action] of at least one externally validated technical artifact at a high bar, such as two peer-reviewed or conference publications, a funded research project, or an open-source contribution with demonstrated traction such as 500+ downloads; the artifact must identify the candidate's technical contribution.
axes.moderate_criteria: Active ownership [action] of one publication, conference paper, funded project, or released open-source artifact with some concrete external evidence, but below the strong level in count, selectivity, funding, or adoption. A course project, peripheral contribution, or tool listing alone does not qualify.
